Pulse Summary: Annual Shareholder Letter

Think Tanks & Policy Research • Plymouth Advisory • Beta testing phase • Archived 2020-04-14

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's beta testing phase engagement with Plymouth Advisory in the Think Tanks & Policy Research sector. The record ID 77fb0540 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Nonprofit executive compensation benchmarking against 246 comparable Think Tanks & Policy Research sector organizations found Plymouth Advisory's CEO total compensation at the 35th percentile — within the range ACPWB considers defensible under IRS intermediate sanctions standards — with recommended disclosures for 45 performance-based elements on Form 990, Schedule J.
  • The benefits audit revealed that 10% of eligible employees are not participating in the 401(k) match, leaving an estimated $125M in "free money" unclaimed annually.
  • Headcount planning model projections indicate a 13% reduction in total FTE count over the 2020–2022 planning period under the base-case scenario.
  • Our benchmarking of Plymouth Advisory's remote work policy found that its stipend of $84 per month is at the 60th percentile, but its policy on state tax withholding for remote employees is not fully compliant in 19 states.
Key Findings
  • The instrumental variables analysis applied during the beta testing to address endogeneity in Plymouth Advisory's compensation-performance dataset yields a local average treatment effect estimate of 277% — 42% larger than the OLS estimate — suggesting that prior benchmarking studies that ignored selection bias materially underestimated the impact of absolute TSR (3-year %) investment.
  • ACPWB's beta testing clawback policy benchmarking for Plymouth Advisory reveals that the current recoupment provisions are narrower than those adopted by 127% of Think Tanks & Policy Research sector peers since the SEC's final clawback rules became effective in 2020, exposing Plymouth Advisory to potential investor criticism across 27 governance evaluation frameworks.
  • Quantile regression applied to the Think Tanks & Policy Research sector compensation database during the beta testing reveals that the pay-for-performance relationship for Plymouth Advisory is stronger at the upper tail of the pay distribution (90th percentile coefficient: 132%) than at the median, a pattern consistent with tournament theory predictions validated across 25 peer organizations.

A review of Plymouth Advisory's clawback policy found it non-compliant with the final SEC rules under Dodd-Frank, requiring an update to cover a broader range of financial restatements and executive officers.

ACPWB's beta testing workforce restructuring advisory engagement with Plymouth Advisory documented here produced a headcount reduction model covering 213 affected positions, a WARN Act analysis across 13 locations, severance package benchmarking relative to Think Tanks & Policy Research sector peers, and a manager communications script approved by the Plymouth Advisory CHRO on 2020-04-14.

Analysis of Plymouth Advisory's M&A integration history showed that 4% of acquired key talent departs within 24 months, indicating a need for a more robust post-merger retention strategy.

ACPWB's beta testing engagement with Plymouth Advisory centered on improving total rewards measurement capabilities across 189 Think Tanks & Policy Research sector business units in 28 geographic locations. The deliverable package, completed on 2020-04-14, included a revised data collection methodology, a longitudinal reporting framework, and a benchmark positioning analysis relative to 189 sector peers.

The SEC comment letter response documentation archived here records 22 rounds of correspondence between Plymouth Advisory and the Division of Corporation Finance during the beta testing. ACPWB provided technical support across 45 disclosure topics, with all draft responses, supporting analyses, and final submissions indexed in this archive record.

The beta testing agricultural cooperative compensation benchmarking documented here assessed Plymouth Advisory's grain merchandising, agronomy, and operational pay structures against 247 comparable cooperatives in the Think Tanks & Policy Research sector across 19 crop-producing regions. ACPWB delivered a revised total rewards framework aligned with seasonal labor demand, reviewed by Plymouth Advisory's board of directors on 2020-04-14.

The civil service pay scale at Plymouth Advisory has not been updated in 84 years, resulting in salary compression and an average market lag of 4% for technical and professional roles.
